issue.title: Who gets the £100 energy payment: every home in bands A to D, or those in need?
issue.question: The £100 energy payment goes to homes in council tax bands A to D in England. Should it go to every home in those bands, or be aimed at the households who struggle most?
issue.summary: On 24 November 2026 the government set out a £100 Household Energy Payment for up to 20 million households in England in council tax bands A to D. About 13 million are due to be paid automatically, councils start paying on 4 January, and the scheme stays open until the end of May. A separate £100 million fund lets councils help vulnerable households outside the main scheme and set their own rules for it (s1). Homes in bands E to H are left out of the main payment, so some low-income households miss out while some better-off homes in bands A to D are paid (s2). Cornwall Insight forecasts that the January price cap will rise 26%, from £1,723 to £2,166 for a typical household. That is not an official figure, and Ofgem was due to announce the real one on 25 November (s3).
issue.slot_reason: The first energy issue, on 17 November, predicted that Ofgem's January price cap would top £2,000 a year, and that check falls due on 30 November. Today, 25 November, is the day Ofgem is due to announce the cap, and yesterday the government published the rules for the £100 payment meant to soften the rise.

tests.text: Fewer cold households that can't pay get missed, if the money is aimed at need.
Payments reach people without a fight over forms: quick and simple to claim.
Renters in bigger or worse homes outside bands A to D get help too.
Older people who are cold get help without a fight over forms.
Low-income homes in bands E to H aren't left out.
Nobody has to prove they're poor to get the payment.
The money doesn't stop halfway through winter.

voices.text: Pensioners first, especially older renters. Don't make me apply by phone.

bench.title: Make councils' £100m fund pay low-income homes in bands E to H
bench.answer: Keep the £100 for bands A to D and the councils' £100 million fund. Change one rule. In 20 councils drawn by lot from volunteers, the fund must pay £100 to low-income homes in bands E to H, with no form. Other councils run the fund as now, so nobody gets less than today. Provisional fail number: fewer than 8 in 10 eligible homes paid by 31 March 2027. Stops 30 June 2027 unless Parliament votes to keep it. On a pass, the rule goes to every council. The Energy Secretary answers for it. It leaves out Scotland, Wales and low-income households not on benefits.

bench.title: Let local panels, not councils alone, steer the £100m help fund
bench.answer: Try this in 10 volunteer English councils, drawn by lot. A local panel of residents and advice workers would decide who gets the council's share of the £100 million fund. It would put low-income homes in bands E to H first, with a short, simple claim. Other councils keep today's rules. The main £100 payment stays as planned. By 31 May 2027, measure days to payment and how much reaches bands E to H, against places like it. Provisional fail: fewer than 7 in 10 approved claims paid within 30 days. It stops on 31 May 2027 unless Parliament votes to keep it. The Energy Secretary answers for it. It leaves out Scotland and Wales.

bench.title: Let residents steer help for cold homes in every tax band
bench.answer: Keep the promised £100. Trial extra £100 payments in twelve English councils drawn from volunteers, against twelve keeping today's help. Treasury funds a £10m pot; elected residents, including renters and pensioners, steer access and outreach. Any household struggling to heat its home can claim, whatever its tax band, without income paperwork: online, by post or in person. Pay within ten working days. The council leader answers for delays. Provisionally, fail unless surveys find 20% fewer struggling households missed; report older renters separately. Reserve funding through winter. Stop on 31 May 2027 unless Parliament renews after review; success means national expansion. Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland remain outside this trial. Cold homes need help, not auditions.

rows.test: Test: fewer cold households missed, money aimed at need
rows.note: It aims the money at low-income homes in bands E to H, who miss out on the main payment today. It still misses low-income households not on benefits.

rows.test: Test: quick and simple to claim, no fight over forms
rows.note: It says "no form", but once the unsourced records claim is struck it doesn't say how those homes would be found, so quick and simple isn't shown.

rows.test: Test: renters in bigger or worse homes outside bands A to D get help
rows.note: It pays low-income homes in bands E to H, but doesn't say whether renters who don't pay the council tax bill would count. The main payment goes to whoever is responsible for the bill.

rows.test: Test: older people who are cold get help without forms
rows.note: No form helps older people, but pensioners not on benefits are outside it, and the answer never mentions older people.

rows.test: Limit: low-income homes in bands E to H aren't left out
rows.note: The answer itself leaves out low-income households not on benefits, who are low-income homes in bands E to H. Needs no source: it follows from what the answer says.

rows.test: Limit: nobody has to prove they're poor
rows.note: Nobody is asked to apply or prove anything: the answer says "no form". Needs no source: it follows from what the answer says.

rows.test: Limit: the money doesn't stop halfway through winter
rows.note: Payments are due by 31 March and the rule stops on 30 June 2027, after the winter. Needs no source: it follows from what the answer says.

rows.test: Test: fewer cold households missed, money aimed at need
rows.note: A local panel would put bands E to H low-income homes first, but the fail number measures speed, not whether fewer cold households are missed.

rows.test: Test: quick and simple to claim, no fight over forms
rows.note: It promises a short, simple claim, but its fail line allows up to 3 in 10 approved claims to take over 30 days. Whether that is quick is a judgement.

rows.test: Test: renters in bigger or worse homes outside bands A to D get help
rows.note: The panel would include residents and advice workers, but the answer doesn't say renters outside bands A to D get help.

rows.test: Test: older people who are cold get help without forms
rows.note: Advice workers sit on the panel, but a claim is still needed and older people aren't named.

rows.test: Limit: low-income homes in bands E to H aren't left out
rows.note: Bands E to H low-income homes come "first", not for certain, and the panel sets the rules. Nobody can say yet who would be left out.

rows.test: Limit: nobody has to prove they're poor
rows.note: It needs a claim, and the answer doesn't say what proof the panel would ask for.

rows.test: Limit: the money doesn't stop halfway through winter
rows.note: Claims run to a stop date of 31 May 2027, after the winter. Needs no source: it follows from what the answer says.

rows.test: Test: fewer cold households missed, money aimed at need
rows.note: Any household struggling to heat its home can claim, and its fail number is fewer struggling households missed. Needs no source: it follows from what the answer says.

rows.test: Test: quick and simple to claim, no fight over forms
rows.note: No income paperwork, three ways to claim, payment within ten working days. Needs no source: it follows from what the answer says.

rows.test: Test: renters in bigger or worse homes outside bands A to D get help
rows.note: Open to any household whatever its tax band, and elected residents include renters. Needs no source: it follows from what the answer says.

rows.test: Test: older people who are cold get help without forms
rows.note: Post and in-person claims, no income paperwork, and older renters reported separately. Needs no source: it follows from what the answer says.

rows.test: Limit: low-income homes in bands E to H aren't left out
rows.note: Any band can claim, so low-income homes in bands E to H are in. Needs no source: it follows from what the answer says.

rows.test: Limit: nobody has to prove they're poor
rows.note: It says "without income paperwork". Needs no source: it follows from what the answer says.

rows.test: Limit: the money doesn't stop halfway through winter
rows.note: It says it would reserve funding through winter, but £10m pays £100 to only 100,000 households. If more claim, the pot could run dry.

gate.verdict: None of the three passes every test and limit. C passes six of seven and leaves one unclear (whether £10m lasts); A fails the limit on low-income homes it leaves out; B is mostly unclear because its local panel would set the rules. Facts can't settle who comes first.
